newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S NEW SOCIALIST PM AND CABINET SWORN IN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S NEW SOCIALIST PM AND CABINET SWORN IN.

text.p: Greece's socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis and his new cabinet were sworn in on Wednesday by President Costis Stephanopoulos at the start of their four-year term.

In a televised ceremony, black-clad Orthodox priests chanted a blessing for the new government and Simitis then swore an oath of office. He was followed by his new government's 42 ministers and deputy ministers.
Simitis, 60, won Sunday's national election and has formed a cabinet which mixes experienced ministers with a new generation of reformers who helped to put him in power.

A reserved technocrat who studied economics in Germany and Britain, Simitis steered the socialists safely into a new era when he succeeded party founder and legend Andreas Papandreou as prime minister in January.

The ceremony marked the formal start of the post-Papandreou era, with a new generation socialist leader and his hand-picked cabinet setting a firm pro-Western course and turning their back on Papandreou's unpredictable, anti-Western ways.

Political commentators had predicted the socialists would be torn apart after the departure of Papandreou, who forged the powerful party from various leftist factions after a military junta fell in 1974.
Papandreou, revered by the left, was elected Greece's first socialist prime minister in 1981. He was re-elected in 1985 and 1993 but resigned in poor health in January. He died in June.
Simitis has called on Greeks to work hard, make sacrifices and meet European Union economic targets. He has expressed dismay at Greece's dismal showing in most EU lists.
Simitis, who served in every Papandreou cabinet, challenged his one-time mentor last year, accusing him of being out of touch with the party and autocratic.
After winning the party leadership in June, he gambled on an early election to cement his grip on power and to give him a free hand to pick his own cabinet, leaving no doubt about who was boss.
